title: Roy Williams' 2001 Nagurski and Thorpe Award Double at OU
question: What awards did Roy Williams win at Oklahoma in 2001?
answer: In 2001 Oklahoma safety Roy Williams won both the Bronko Nagurski Trophy as the nation's top defender and the Jim Thorpe Award as the top defensive back. He was the first player ever to win both in the same year.
summary: In 2001 OU safety Roy Williams became the first player to win the Nagurski Trophy and Thorpe Award in one season, the year of his famous Superman play vs Texas.
body: Sooner fans remember the leap. In the 2001 Red River game, Roy Williams flew over the line, knocked the ball loose from Texas quarterback Chris Simms, and watched it fall into the hands of teammate Teddy Lehman for a touchdown that sealed a 14-3 Oklahoma win. That play earned him the nickname Superman, and by December it had company in the trophy case.

Williams won both the Bronko Nagurski Trophy, given to the best defensive player in the country, and the Jim Thorpe Award, given to the best defensive back. According to the National Football Foundation, he was the first player in history to claim both in the same year. He was also a unanimous first-team All-American, Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year, and finished seventh in the Heisman voting, the top finish that year for a non-quarterback.

He helped lead the 2001 Sooners to an 11-2 record capped by a 10-3 Cotton Bowl win over Arkansas, where he was named Defensive MVP. A year earlier he had been part of the unbeaten 2000 team that won the national championship. Across three seasons he totaled 287 tackles, 34 tackles for loss and nine interceptions.
Williams left a year early, and the Dallas Cowboys picked him eighth overall in 2002. He earned five straight Pro Bowl selections from 2003 to 2007 and was a first-team All-Pro in 2003.

He entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 2022 as the 23rd Sooner player so honored. His Roy Williams Safety Net Foundation supports low-income single mothers, and OU's Roy Williams Strength and Speed Complex carries his name.
